assertions.assert: Each element (attention, verdict, stimulus, recognize) takes exactly its declared attributes, the required ones present and none empty, and no content, and the namespace has no other element: a malformed element raises error.execution and assigns nothing (its schema, package/bot.xsd, rejects it before any run under scx validate).

<bot:stimulus> writes the envelope {event, data, source, target?, id?}: event a non-empty string, source null when it evaluates to null, undefined or the empty string, and target and id included when given and not undefined; an empty event raises error.execution and assigns nothing.

<bot:attention> writes the focus (the given focus when it is a configured device, else null) as the first candidate, then the stimulus's device (a bot.input's data.target_device, which the environment stamps on a device's input) when it is configured and not a candidate already; devices that are not an array raise error.execution and assign nothing.

<bot:verdict> writes the selections without bot.ability.cognition.ignore ones, and the original's message for the first one the attention policy refuses (a focus_device outside the candidates or with invalid data, a clear_focus for another target or with no focus), else null.

<bot:recognize> writes true exactly when the name's case-folded letter-and-digit tokens appear as a whole run among the text's; a missing name or one with no tokens is never heard, and a text that is neither a string nor null raises error.execution and assigns nothing.
